correctness.rationale: The sign-drift perturbation bound is proven by the forward invariance of an explicit thin interval and exact motion outside it. Split at m=floor(n/log(n)^4): early drift shrinks as 1/log(n)^2, weighted-sign triangular-array CLT has variance tending to one, late drift mass tends to theta, and late martingale maximal variance tends to zero. The continuous mapping theorem yields the soft-threshold normal limit. A uniform L² envelope yields expectation convergence. An exact monotone integral proves uniqueness of the coefficient optimizer. The standalone finite checker corroborates discrete inequalities and numeric constants, without being treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The existing logarithmic expected-rate lower bound cannot determine whether errors are rare or typical. An explicit nondegenerate limiting distribution with an atom and exact threshold exceedance probabilities supplies a meaningful stochastic-reliability characterization. A sharp leading-order expected-loss constant and a unique natural tuning optimizer benchmark attainable logarithmic loss within a motivated bounded-noise construction; no sweeping minimax optimality is asserted.
